title: 6sense vs Demandbase: Which ABM Platform Fits Your Team
summary: 6sense vs Demandbase compared: predictive buying stages vs native B2B advertising, intent data, pricing models, setup effort, and how to test both.
body_markdown:
## 6sense vs Demandbase: the short answer


Pick 6sense if sales will own the tool and the weekly question is which accounts are moving toward a decision. Its core is a predictive model that assigns each account a buying stage.


Pick Demandbase if marketing will own it and most of your ABM budget goes to ads aimed at a target account list. Its core is a native B2B demand-side platform, so targeting, bidding and measurement happen inside the product.


Both are Leaders in Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for ABM platforms. Both sell intent data, predictive scoring, advertising, web personalization and sales intelligence, and both need enterprise budgets and real setup. The feature list won’t settle it. Which team opens the tool every day, and what it needs answered, usually will.


## Side-by-side comparison


6sense Demandbase


**Core bet** Predict which accounts are in a buying cycle Reach target accounts with account-based ads


**Intent data** Keyword-level research, web visits, partner intent, CRM and marketing activity; Bombora topics as a paid add-on Topic intent plus signal volume from its own ad platform and data partners


**Predictive model** Buying stages from target to purchase, trained on your wins and losses Several predictive models, journey stages configurable per product


**Advertising** Sold as a module, run through DSP partners Native B2B DSP; Advertising can be bought on its own


**Sales intelligence** Separate module, contact reveals on credits Often bundled in higher tiers


**Pricing model** Quote by accounts, modules and data packs Platform fee plus a flat fee per user


**Typical contract** Median around $60,000 a year in Vendr buyer data Similar, slightly higher median


**TrustRadius score** 8.3 out of 10 7.5 out of 10


## Intent data and predictive scoring


Intent is why most teams buy either platform, and the two collect it differently.


6sense groups its signals under what it calls Signalverse: keyword-level research across B2B sites, anonymous website visits matched to accounts, partner intent, and activity from your CRM and marketing automation. Its models turn that into a buying stage per account, from target through awareness, consideration, decision and purchase. Bombora topic intent is listed as an add-on, so check which feeds your quote includes.


Demandbase draws signal volume from its own ad platform, which sees programmatic bidstream traffic, plus partnerships with other intent providers. On scoring it sells flexibility: several predictive models, and journey stages you configure per product. That helps if you sell more than one product into the same accounts.


Two caveats apply to both:


- **The model learns from your CRM.** If opportunity stages are inconsistent or closed-lost reasons are blank, either platform learns the wrong lessons.
- **An intent spike isn’t a buying decision.** Topic activity can come from research, education or someone with no role in the purchase. IP-based matching also struggles with remote workers.


One sales leader we spoke with dropped one of these platforms because its intent signals were too surface-level to change which deals reps worked.


## Advertising and sales intelligence


Demandbase runs its own demand-side platform built for B2B and sells Advertising as a starting point, so a team can buy account-based ads first and add the rest of the platform later. If your program warms accounts with display ads before outbound, that control over spend is the main reason to pick it.


6sense sells advertising as a module and typically runs programmatic through DSP partners. Ads are a smaller part of 6sense than of Demandbase.


On sales features the order reverses. 6sense sells Sales Intelligence as its own product, with company and contact data, recommended contacts and CRM alerts, and contact reveals run on credits. Demandbase often bundles sales intelligence into higher tiers and doesn’t split the platform into separate sales and marketing products.


So with 6sense you can scope a deal around sales seats and credits. With Demandbase you buy one platform for both teams.


## Pricing and setup effort


Neither vendor publishes a rate card. Vendr’s buyer data puts the median contract for both around $60,000 a year, with Demandbase slightly higher. Your account count, seats, modules and ad budget move the number more than the vendor name does.


- **6sense** quotes by the number of accounts you monitor, the modules you add and the data packs you buy.
- **Demandbase** charges a platform fee for the core software and services, plus a flat fee per user.


Budget separately for implementation and onboarding, and for someone to own the platform for at least the first quarter. CRM and marketing automation sync, website tags, segments, ad audiences and score thresholds that sales agrees with all take time. Reviewers split on which is easier to set up. 6sense says its models need less manual tuning, and Demandbase says its setup is more configurable. Either way, someone on your team has to maintain the models or learn to trust them.


One sales leader we spoke with worried that every point tool is turning into an all-in-one platform. Before you sign, list which features overlap with tools you already pay for, such as a contact database, a sequencer or an ad platform.


## How to test both before you sign


Each vendor publishes a comparison page about the other. Treat both as sales material and run your own test:


1. **Run both on the same accounts.** Give each vendor the same target list, including accounts that became closed-won deals in the last two quarters. The platform that flagged more of them before the opportunity opened has the more useful signal for your market.
2. **Get the advertising split in writing.** Ask for the platform fee versus working media at your planned spend.
3. **Decide who owns first touch.** A pattern we see: marketing runs the intent program, sales runs outbound, and nobody owns the account the platform flags. Settle that before rollout.
4. **Plan where the signal lives.** Teams that run an ABM platform next to other signal sources end up with alerts in too many tools and no playbook. The ones that make it work pull every signal into the CRM and rank accounts where several signals overlap first.
5. **Believe the rep who talks about fit.** I once spoke with a former AE at a long-established enterprise vendor who told buyers to hear out a newer challenger. His product suited large, risk-averse teams, and he said so when it didn’t suit theirs. Buyers trusted him more for it. If a 6sense or Demandbase rep tells you the other platform fits part of your use case better, take it seriously.


## What neither platform tells you


Both platforms show accounts researching your category. Neither tells you which competitor an account is evaluating, or that an evaluation has already started.


That gap costs most in enterprise deals. One enterprise sales leader told us their reps get added late to RFPs as a check-the-box vendor, after a competitor already shaped the evaluation. Topic research rarely surfaces that early enough.
